notes: מְרִיבַת הָעֵדָה is rendered arthrously (*the strife of the congregation*), so nothing is fronted: the article takes the *the* standing before its own word and the construct takes a supplied one (rule 29).
הֵם מֵי־מְרִיבַת קָדֵשׁ is a verbless clause: *These* to the explicit pronoun and the construction-supplied copula to the predicate מֵי (rule 20).
פִּי is a bare direct object with no marker or preposition on it, so the supplied *against* is the preposition by which the English verb reaches its object and belongs to the verb's unit (rule 44).
